candidates.title: Civitai prompt 144673172
candidates.prompt:
A tall portrait illustration in 4:5 proportion, 1600 pixels wide by 2000 tall.

Image 1 is attached for style only. Take from it the drawing and painting method. The line is a dark sepia-black brush ink of medium weight, a little wobbly, tapering at its ends, and every shape is closed by its own contour. Interior lines are few: one long stroke for a fold, a short tick for a crack or a knuckle. Colour is flat fill laid inside the lines, watercolour over gouache, and each fill carries soft mottled blooms, a few darker tide-marks and a fine speckled cold-press paper grain. Changes of value arrive as big soft wash patches, such as paler streaks across a dark cloth. Every shape's interior is flat wash, and every surface is matte. Leave behind everything Image 1 depicts: its hooded figure, its embrace, its red-haired woman and ruffled gown, its gargoyle, its tombs and graveyard, and its brick-red sky. This picture holds one figure alone on a stone balcony under a muted green sky.

The composition is one hooked line. Her arm reaches out from the shoulder, turns up at the elbow, and the forearm points to the saucer and the moon. A woman stands behind a stone balustrade whose top cuts across her just below the waist. Her body is turned three-quarters toward image-right and her face is tipped up toward the moon. The top of her head is 21% down from the top edge, her chin 38% down, and her head is centred 40% across. The moon is a full cream disc in the upper-right corner zone, centred 78% across and 15% down, a quarter of the picture's width in diameter, with green sky on every side of it.

Her left arm, the one farther from the viewer, on the image-right side of her body, makes the offering. It is drawn whole against the green sky. Her upper arm reaches out and down from the shoulder to the elbow at 74% across and 54% down. Her forearm rises from the elbow almost straight up, and her hand is at 70% across and 30% down, palm turned up and tilted back toward the viewer, holding the saucer just below and a little to the image-left of the moon. A strip of green sky about a third of the saucer's width separates the saucer's top edge from the moon's lower rim. Her right arm, nearer the viewer, hangs on the image-left side of her body with the elbow bent, and her right hand lies flat on the balustrade top at 30% across and 78% down.

The quiet detail for a second look: the saucer carries one hairline crack that runs from its upper-right rim, the edge nearest the moon, down and toward the left. On the moon's lower-left rim, one short ink hairline, no longer than a fifth of the moon's width, runs inward from the rim toward the moon's centre. Seen together, the two hairlines lie on one slanting line pointing from the saucer to the middle of the moon, with a strip of sky between them. The rest of the moon is a plain, unmarked cream disc with a thin ochre rim.

The woman is an adult vampire who looks about thirty-eight. Her face is long and narrow, with a strong brow ridge, a jaw that narrows to a firm chin, and a long neck. Her nose is one wobbly hooked line with a slight bump at the bridge. Each eyelid is one curved lash stroke with a thin dark crescent of iris beneath it, so her eyes are half lowered and fixed on the moon. Her mouth is a single closed line. Her left brow, on the image-right, sits higher than her right, and a short ink tick cuts through its tail. The tip of one canine rests on her lower lip at the image-left corner of her mouth. Her skin is a flat pale peach fill, an even colour across both cheeks, with a greyer wash patch on the side away from the moon. Her black hair is pinned up in a low knot at the back of her head. She is still and unhurried, chin lifted, shoulders square, her expression patient.

She wears a sepia-black gown with a narrow band collar at the base of her throat, closed down the front with a row of small ochre buttons, and long sleeves to the wrist. A deep red cape is clasped at her throat with one plain ochre disc and hangs behind her at image-left in three or four large angular shapes, with a darker rust lining showing in one fold. One long red fall of the cape hangs from the underside of her raised left elbow down toward the balustrade. Her left forearm, wrist and hand stand bare of cloth against the green sky, with plain sky on both sides of the saucer.

The saucer is a small porcelain saucer, 12% of the picture's width across, a little wider than her palm, resting on her palm and fingertips with her thumb at its rim. Its inside well faces the viewer and the moon and shows as a flat ellipse, wider than it is tall. It is a cool pale grey-white, a shade greyer than the moon, inked in sepia-black with a thin ochre line round the rim. One ink hairline starts at a small chipped notch on the upper-right rim, runs two thirds of the way across the well toward the lower left, and ends in one short forked tick. The well is empty. Apart from that crack, the saucer is a flat plain dish, a plain unmarked rim and a plain unmarked well, one flat fill, held alone in her hand.

The setting is a balcony at night.
